# Dedication

For my father, Richard Smith. You taught chemistry, biology, and physics, but what you really taught was a way of seeing. I grew up watching you read, think, and form opinions grounded in learning. You paired curiosity with humility. You believed that looking into a microscope could move a person toward God. One day on a field trip with your students in the Delta, taking core samples on a small boat, I watched your love of discovery come alive. I will never forget it.

Your example gave me reverence for the Earth and planted the seeds for my life's work in renewables and land. You encouraged us to learn, to think for ourselves, and to speak with care. You were the most well-rounded person I knew because you never stopped growing.

My parents are gone now, yet your voice is here on every page. This book is part of the legacy you gave me. A love of knowledge. A sense of wonder. And faith that what we steward is a gift. I hope to pass that on to my grandchildren, just as you passed it on to me.
